svg.aria-label: Gerege IdP MVP system architecture: browsers, a terminal and an IoT device reach an Istio ingress gateway; the gateway and every application sidecar call one Go external authorizer over gRPC, which answers from SpiceDB; Keycloak provides identity only.
svg.font-family: Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.text: Every request into an application passes an Envoy sidecar that consults one Go authorizer, which answers from SpiceDB. Keycloak only says who you are — and an agent holding your token is bound by what you delegated, not by what you can do.
opaque session cookie — never a token
internal hop — authorized again at the callee
KIND CLUSTER · gerege-idp · kubernetes v1.36.1 · one node · host :80 → NodePort 30080
profile · smarthome · account · device → workloads below
id.local.test → Keycloak — deliberately NOT sent to ext-authz
PeerAuthentication STRICT downstream: mTLS to every sidecar
an IoT device, holding only a token
own telemetry ✓ · thermostat-1 ✗ · alice's profile ✗ · no token ✗
consent declared but suppressed — a user acting on their own data through their own app
sa/profile-service · profile data API, internal only
no authorization logic in this service. look for it: there is none
consent enforced — the azp claim is the only thing that differs
RFC 8693 exchange: sub stays alice, azp becomes the agent — then it acts, bound by the delegation
/internal/* callable only by smarthome-service and agent-runner; /telemetry only by the device
Every internal hop is authorized again at the callee's own sidecar — the same identities, a different question.
A gateway-only architecture never gets to ask the second one.
the identity and authorization plane · STRICT mTLS on account-app
Go · envoy.service.auth.v3 gRPC :9001 · the decision point
OIDC callback and logout — before any authorization
principal ← bearer token, or session → token
match a route rule — no match → DENY
is this workload registered for this application?
emit a decision record — principal AND actor
read-only on SpiceDB · no decision cache · every error path denies
22 rules · defaultAction DENY · health :9002 · decision log :9003 (pod-only)
Fail-closed by construction: failOpen: false at the mesh · defaultAction DENY in the route document · every error branch in ext-authz returns a denial · SpiceDB unreachable → nothing is permitted.

An agent adds one actor, one grant and one gate: it is registered rather than inferred · its authority is an expiring delegation, not the token it holds · and a step-up route refuses it outright, because it cannot re-authenticate the person behind it.
